question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

 
The matrix $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=1.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $A=PD{P}^{-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we are already given the eigenvalues of the matrix: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=2,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=1.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ Applying our usual method, we find the following.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives us the eigenverctor ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives us the eigenverctor ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{3}=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)x=0$ gives us the eigenverctor ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
